newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam coffee market steady as deals dry up.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam coffee market steady as deals dry up.

text.p: Vietnam's robusta coffee prices were little changed this week as both buyers and sellers sat on the sidelines, traders said.
"The market really is frozen now," said one trader. "There's no buying interest and farmers are still sitting on stock in the hope that prices will go back up."
Traders said the market was currently at around $1,350-1,370 a tonne, FOB Saigon Port, up about $20 from a week ago.
However, sellers were reported to be looking for higher prices after bids went as high as $1,480 a tonne earlier this month.
"Sellers are a bit on the high side at the moment. Compared to the terminal market, it's a bit unrealistic," said one trader.
Traders say some 200,000 tonnes of coffee has been sold from the 1996/97 (Oct-Sept) crop, which they estimated at about 270,000-280,000 tonnes.
